claims.claim: Adam Roberts characterises Wolfe's four-part novel as baroquely iterated and patterned, treating the baroque quality as a virtue rather than a fault.
claims.source: Adam Roberts, 'Gene Wolfe, The Book of the New Sun (1980-83)', Adam's Notebook (Medium), 3 July 2023
claims.quote: fluently rendered, baroquely iterated and patterned
claims.page: body, after the plot summary opening
claims.polarity: asserts the baroque label, rejects it as a defect

claims.claim: Roberts reports that some critics have called Wolfe obscure.
claims.source: Adam Roberts, Adam's Notebook (Medium), 3 July 2023
claims.quote: Wolfe has been called obscure by some critics
claims.polarity: reports the charge, then disputes it

claims.claim: Roberts states he is not persuaded by Peter Wright's thesis that a deliberate obscurity is the heart of Wolfe's art.
claims.source: Adam Roberts, Adam's Notebook (Medium), 3 July 2023
claims.quote: I am not persuaded by this thesis
claims.page: footnote on Peter Wright's Attending Daedalus
claims.polarity: rejects the obscurity-as-method thesis

claims.claim: Roberts relays Peter Wright's charge that Wolfe confounds the reader by style, allusion and misdirection.
claims.source: Adam Roberts relaying Peter Wright, Attending Daedalus (Liverpool UP 2003), in Adam's Notebook, 3 July 2023
claims.quote: confounds the reader
claims.page: footnote on Peter Wright's Attending Daedalus
claims.polarity: relays a hostile characterisation Roberts himself rejects

claims.claim: Roberts says Wolfe prefers to signify by inflection and suggestion rather than by direct statement.
claims.source: Adam Roberts, Adam's Notebook (Medium), 3 July 2023
claims.quote: preferring to signify by inflection and suggestion than direct
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'Wolfe finesses his meaning'
claims.polarity: asserts the device and defends it

claims.claim: Roberts contrasts Wolfe with Stephen Donaldson, calling Wolfe's terminology always precise and always appropriate.
claims.source: Adam Roberts, Adam's Notebook (Medium), 3 July 2023
claims.quote: terminology is always precise, always appropriate
claims.polarity: rejects the overwritten charge for Wolfe while applying it to Donaldson

claims.claim: Roberts says a full summary of the plot here would be dense, overbusy and baffling.
claims.source: Adam Roberts, Adam's Notebook (Medium), 3 July 2023
claims.quote: a full summary here would be dense, overbusy, baffling
claims.polarity: concedes the plot's difficulty

claims.claim: Bebergal writes that far more people own a copy of The Book of the New Sun than have read it all the way through.
claims.source: Peter Bebergal, 'Sci-Fi's Difficult Genius', The New Yorker, 24 April 2015
claims.quote: far more people own a copy than have read it
claims.page: body, paragraph comparing the book to Ulysses
claims.polarity: asserts the difficulty as a barrier

claims.claim: Bebergal describes the four books of the series as sometimes vexing.
claims.source: Peter Bebergal, The New Yorker, 24 April 2015
claims.quote: The four books that make up the series are sometimes vexing
claims.polarity: asserts the difficulty

claims.claim: Bebergal says Wolfe dredges up truly obscure words, naming cataphract, fuligin, metamynodon and cacogens.
claims.source: Peter Bebergal, The New Yorker, 24 April 2015
claims.quote: dredges up some truly obscure words: cataphract, fuligin, metamynodon, cacogens
claims.page: body, paragraph on the strangeness of English
claims.polarity: asserts obscure diction as a difficulty

claims.claim: Bebergal reports that a reader can become convinced of having cracked a riddle only for the answer to fail to illuminate the rest of the story.
claims.source: Peter Bebergal, The New Yorker, 24 April 2015
claims.quote: the answer fails to illuminate the rest of the story
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'Reading The Book of the New Sun is dizzying'
claims.polarity: asserts that the withholding does not always pay off

claims.claim: Bebergal says Wolfe does not reveal the truth behind any of the central mysteries explicitly.
claims.source: Peter Bebergal, The New Yorker, 24 April 2015
claims.quote: doesn't reveal the truth behind any of the central mysteries
claims.polarity: asserts the device

claims.claim: Bebergal writes that truth of any kind is hard to come by in Wolfe's books no matter how closely one reads.
claims.source: Peter Bebergal, The New Yorker, 24 April 2015
claims.quote: is hard to come by in Wolfe's books
claims.polarity: asserts the limit of close reading

claims.claim: Bebergal says Wolfe's plots are unspooled by narrators who deliberately confuse or are confused.
claims.source: Peter Bebergal, The New Yorker, 24 April 2015
claims.quote: narrators who deliberately confuse or are confused
claims.polarity: asserts the device

claims.claim: Bebergal writes that Wolfe has rarely if ever been considered fully within the larger context of literature.
claims.source: Peter Bebergal, The New Yorker, 24 April 2015
claims.quote: rarely, if ever, been considered fully within the larger context
claims.polarity: asserts the marginal reception

claims.claim: Bebergal reports that Wolfe told him Latro's memory loss does not make him an unreliable narrator, contrary to what many critics assume.
claims.source: Peter Bebergal paraphrasing Gene Wolfe by telephone, The New Yorker, 24 April 2015
claims.quote: does not make him an unreliable narrator, as many critics assume
claims.polarity: the author disputes the critics' label

claims.claim: Peter Wright relays Algis Budrys's F and SF review admitting he cannot follow Wolfe's moves and knows the cards are up the sleeves somewhere.
claims.source: Peter Wright relaying Algis Budrys, review in Magazine of Fantasy and Science Fiction, cited as June 1980 p. 49; Ultan's Library, 28 August 2002
claims.quote: I know the cards are up the sleeves somewhere
claims.polarity: relays a sceptical reviewer's charge of deception

claims.claim: Peter Wright relays Baird Searles asking whether under the glittering edifice of surprising words there is a story or a concept of any stature.
claims.source: Peter Wright relaying Baird Searles, review of The Citadel of the Autarch, Isaac Asimov's Science Fiction Magazine, May 1983, p. 167; Ultan's Library, 28 August 2002
claims.quote: is there a story or a concept of any stature?
claims.polarity: relays the charge that the manner outruns the matter

claims.claim: Peter Wright relays Baird Searles's judgement that The Book of the New Sun marks a turning point of science fiction from content to style, from matter to manner.
claims.source: Peter Wright relaying Baird Searles, Isaac Asimov's Science Fiction Magazine, May 1983, p. 167; Ultan's Library, 28 August 2002
claims.quote: from content to style, from matter to manner
claims.polarity: relays a sceptical framing of the book's stylistic turn

claims.claim: Peter Wright argues that critics have extolled The Book of the New Sun for its fluidity of style rather than engaging with the text to any meaningful degree.
claims.source: Peter Wright, 'Mapping a Masterwork', Ultan's Library, 28 August 2002
claims.quote: Rather than engaging with the text to any meaningful degree
claims.polarity: disputes the quality of the praise the prose has received

claims.claim: Peter Wright calls the existing claims for viewing Wolfe's tetralogy as a masterpiece somewhat flimsy and subjective.
claims.source: Peter Wright, 'Mapping a Masterwork', Ultan's Library, 28 August 2002
claims.quote: somewhat flimsy and subjective
claims.polarity: disputes the received praise

claims.claim: Peter Wright notes that Wolfe's appendix calls the obscure nouns of his translation intended to be suggestive rather than definitive.
claims.source: Peter Wright quoting Gene Wolfe's appendix to The Shadow of the Torturer (Arrow 1981, p. 302); Ultan's Library, 28 August 2002
claims.quote: intended to be suggestive rather than definitive
claims.polarity: relays the author's own account of his diction

claims.claim: A reader commenting under Wright's review objects that Wright spent three thousand words on the books' density without providing a single example.
claims.source: commenter 'Charles L' on Peter Wright's review, Ultan's Library, 9 May 2015
claims.quote: without providing a single example
claims.polarity: disputes the critical case for the prose

claims.claim: David Auerbach writes that striking bits and pieces of The Book of the New Sun stayed with him but the work as a whole has not.
claims.source: David Auerbach, 'Gene Wolfe: The Book of the New Sun', Waggish, 23 November 2007
claims.quote: the work as a whole has not
claims.polarity: asserts the book fails as a whole

claims.claim: Auerbach says Wolfe employs a somewhat high-falutin style using words that appear to be neologisms but are drawn from archaic usages.
claims.source: David Auerbach, Waggish, 23 November 2007
claims.quote: a somewhat high-falutin' style using words that appear to be neologisms
claims.polarity: asserts the diction is mannered

claims.claim: Auerbach reports that some readers he knows find Wolfe's style insufferably pompous and awkward.
claims.source: David Auerbach reporting acquaintances, Waggish, 23 November 2007
claims.quote: find the resulting style insufferably pompous and awkward
claims.polarity: relays the overwritten charge without endorsing it

claims.claim: Auerbach judges that Wolfe's style does not make the writing beautiful.
claims.source: David Auerbach, Waggish, 23 November 2007
claims.quote: What it doesn't do is make the writing beautiful
claims.polarity: disputes the claim that Wolfe's prose is beautiful

claims.claim: Auerbach calls Wolfe's prose clunky in a way that cannot be ignored, contrasting it with Philip K. Dick's clunky but self-effacing style.
claims.source: David Auerbach, Waggish, 23 November 2007
claims.quote: Wolfe's is clunky, and it can't be ignored
claims.polarity: asserts the prose is a defect

claims.claim: Auerbach says central plot points in Wolfe are skipped over and only referred to in retrospect.
claims.source: David Auerbach, Waggish, 23 November 2007
claims.quote: Central plot points are skipped over and only referred to in retrospect
claims.page: section beginning 'The next issue is the plot'
claims.polarity: asserts the elision device and treats it as a problem

claims.claim: Auerbach argues the book is underdetermined because the reader cannot know the intent behind Severian's lies and so cannot derive the meaning of any particular piece from the whole.
claims.source: David Auerbach, Waggish, 23 November 2007
claims.quote: we can't derive from the whole what the meaning of
claims.page: section beginning 'But where the book most seriously fails'
claims.polarity: asserts that the withholding defeats inference

claims.claim: Auerbach calls Wolfe's instability of text an intentional choice that indicates a serious failure to push the book past the realm of entertainment.
claims.source: David Auerbach, Waggish, 23 November 2007
claims.quote: indicates a serious failure on the part of Wolfe
claims.page: section beginning 'But where the book most seriously fails'
claims.polarity: rejects the withholding as a success

claims.claim: Auerbach contrasts Wolfe unfavourably with Christopher Priest, who places unreliable narrators within a determinate context.
claims.source: David Auerbach, Waggish, 23 November 2007
claims.quote: is sure to place them within a determinate
claims.polarity: rejects Wolfe's handling of unreliable narration by comparison

claims.claim: Auerbach says Wolfe uses unreliability devices without appearing to have a larger sense of what they might mean, calling them just a game.
claims.source: David Auerbach, Waggish, 23 November 2007
claims.quote: like the lesser Oulipo novels, they're just a game
claims.polarity: rejects the device as purposeful

claims.claim: Auerbach names elisions, subtle inconsistencies and deliberate withholding of information as the grounds for distrusting Severian.
claims.source: David Auerbach replying in comments, Waggish, 6 January 2008
claims.quote: elisions, subtle inconsistencies, and deliberate withholding of information
claims.polarity: asserts the device

claims.claim: A commenter on Auerbach's post says the analysis names why they never got into Wolfe despite Wolfe plainly making a huge effort.
claims.source: commenter 'mrs gaw' on Waggish, 25 November 2007
claims.quote: why I never got into Wolfe
claims.polarity: endorses the counter-case

claims.claim: Auerbach argues that Wolfe subordinates thematic and conceptual integrity to the mere challenge of his narrative games.
claims.source: David Auerbach, 'More on Gene Wolfe', Waggish, 7 December 2007
claims.quote: subordinates thematic and conceptual integrity to the mere challenge
claims.page: body, paragraph comparing Wolfe with Joyce
claims.polarity: rejects the device as purposeful

claims.claim: Auerbach says that by The Book of the New Sun the elisions have multiplied beyond what he can manage.
claims.source: David Auerbach, 'More on Gene Wolfe', Waggish, 7 December 2007
claims.quote: the elisions have multiplied beyond what I can manage
claims.polarity: asserts the withholding exceeds the reader's capacity

claims.claim: Auerbach quotes Wolfe's own statement that he tries not to leave a clue more than once.
claims.source: David Auerbach quoting Gene Wolfe from the James B. Jordan interview, Waggish, 7 December 2007
claims.quote: I try not to leave a clue more than once
claims.polarity: relays the author's stated method

claims.claim: Auerbach relays James B. Jordan's report that Orson Scott Card reviewed a Wolfe soldier novel saying he could not figure out what the book was about.
claims.source: David Auerbach quoting James B. Jordan's interview question relaying Orson Scott Card, Waggish, 7 December 2007
claims.quote: I can't figure out what this book is about
claims.polarity: relays a hostile reader verdict

claims.claim: Auerbach describes Wolfe's books as machines that give trouble only when one looks for the animating spirit.
claims.source: David Auerbach, 'More on Gene Wolfe', Waggish, 7 December 2007
claims.quote: it is only when looking for the animating spirit
claims.polarity: asserts a mechanical quality as a limitation

claims.claim: Critic Ray Davis comments that Wolfe is simply not managing to do the job he wants to do.
claims.source: Ray Davis in comments on Waggish, 8 December 2007
claims.quote: he's simply not managing to do the job he wants to do
claims.polarity: endorses the counter-case

claims.claim: The reviewer bormgans reports that on rereading The Book of the New Sun was to a certain extent a lesser affair than he remembered.
claims.source: bormgans, 'THE BOOK OF THE NEW SUN - Gene Wolfe (1980-83)', Weighing a pig doesn't fatten it, 16 May 2021
claims.quote: I have to admit that to a certain extent is was
claims.polarity: reports a downgraded verdict on reread

claims.claim: bormgans quotes and rejects Auerbach's conclusion that the instability of the text is a serious failure by Wolfe.
claims.source: bormgans quoting David Auerbach, Weighing a pig doesn't fatten it, 16 May 2021
claims.quote: I don't agree with Auerbach's conclusion however
claims.page: section on the three reasons interpretation is difficult
claims.polarity: disputes the counter-case

claims.claim: bormgans argues it is not possible to solve all the puzzles in The Book of the New Sun and suspects Wolfe made that deliberately impossible.
claims.source: bormgans, Weighing a pig doesn't fatten it, 16 May 2021
claims.quote: I don't think it is possible to solve all the puzzles
claims.page: section on the three reasons interpretation is difficult
claims.polarity: asserts the withholding is unresolvable

claims.claim: bormgans calls Peter Wright's Ultan's Library review a rather hagiographic text.
claims.source: bormgans on Peter Wright's review, Weighing a pig doesn't fatten it, 16 May 2021
claims.quote: has written a rather hagiographic text on the subject
claims.polarity: disputes the critical defence

claims.claim: bormgans reports finding the text perfectly enjoyable without trying to figure out the obscure words.
claims.source: bormgans, Weighing a pig doesn't fatten it, 16 May 2021
claims.quote: I found the text perfectly enjoyable without trying to figure out
claims.polarity: rejects the charge that the diction blocks reading

claims.claim: bormgans relays Marc Aramini's observation that critical discourse on Wolfe is marked by how infrequently any two people agree with each other.
claims.source: bormgans quoting Marc Aramini's review of Andre-Driussi's Chapter Guide (2019), Weighing a pig doesn't fatten it, 16 May 2021
claims.quote: how infrequently any two people will agree with each other
claims.page: section on the three reasons interpretation is difficult
claims.polarity: asserts interpretive non-convergence

claims.claim: bormgans writes in the comments that there is something of a one-trick pony vibe to Wolfe's writing.
claims.source: bormgans in comments, Weighing a pig doesn't fatten it, 17 May 2021
claims.quote: there's something of a one-trick pony vibe to his writing
claims.polarity: disputes Wolfe's range

claims.claim: A commenter says reviews of this kind keep them shying away from Gene Wolfe.
claims.source: commenter 'Riders of Skaith', Weighing a pig doesn't fatten it, 17 May 2021
claims.quote: It's reviews like like this that keep me shying away
claims.polarity: reports deterrence by the book's reputation for difficulty

claims.claim: The reviewer Jesse calls The Book of the New Sun divisive for its relative opacity.
claims.source: Jesse, Speculiction, 9 July 2012
claims.quote: Divisive for its relative opacity
claims.polarity: asserts the opacity divides readers

claims.claim: Jesse says readers who prefer a narrator who leads them by the hand may withdraw in consternation from Wolfe's unreliable narration.
claims.source: Jesse, Speculiction, 9 July 2012
claims.quote: may withdraw in consternation confronting
claims.polarity: asserts the device costs readers
